I will choose the movie!
All right, then I will swing by home to change clothes and head to the movie theater.
Yes, I will stop by the station, get ready quickly, and head right over.
Got it!
Yeah, visiting a friend's house today was a first for me too—bye!
Did the battery die?
There is something I really must tell you, so I am right outside your house, Producer.
Ah Ms. Cindy, I actually have plans right now…
I will wait for you.

meanings.note: Basic verb of motion. With the respectful ending -세요 in 안녕히 가세요, it forms the polite farewell 'Goodbye!'. RR: gada.

examples.trans: I am going home.
Go safely!

meanings.note: Used as connective -고 (갈아입고).

examples.text: 그래, 그럼 나는 집에 잠깐 가서 옷을 갈아입고 영화관으로 가지 뭐.
examples.trans: All right, then I will swing by home to change clothes and head to the movie theater.
Let us do that (changing into and) right away.

meanings.note: Bound noun often contracted to 거 in everyday speech.

examples.trans: This is my bag.
Because I think I'm late.

examples.text: 너 나 기분 좋게 해서 결제 받으려고 이러는 거잖아. 나 이만 원밖에 없다.
examples.trans: You are just flattering me to collect today's installment, right? I only have twenty thousand won today.
The topic of payment, settlement came up during this shoot.

meanings.note: dummy

examples.trans: dummy trans 1
dummy trans 2

meanings.note: Colloquial contraction of 그러면.

examples.trans: Then let's meet tomorrow.
Then we're at the same company!

meanings.note: With future or present-progressive verbs, means 'right away / in a moment'.
With past-tense verbs, means 'just now'.

examples.trans: I'll be right there.
I just arrived a moment ago.
I want to wait right now.
How about trying to wait together tomorrow?

meanings.note: Emphasizes necessity or strong intention.
Used with holding or closing actions.

examples.trans: Definitely contact me tomorrow.
Please close the door tightly.

meanings.note: Plain first-person singular pronoun used with friends, younger people, or subordinates; contracts to 난 with -는 and becomes 내가 before -가.

examples.trans: I'm going to stay home today.
I'll go first.

나가다.gloss: to go out, to step outside

meanings.en: to go out, to step outside, to leave a room
meanings.note: 나- ('out') + 가다 ('to go')

examples.trans: Let's step outside for a moment and talk.
He went out of the conference room.
Do you have time today?
Where are you going?

meanings.note: Used only with close friends, younger people, or children

examples.trans: Did you hear about this just as?
I was busy today because of just as.
Did you hear about this big hit?
I was busy today because of big hit.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (verb).

examples.text: 저는 짐 갖다 놓고 가려고 잠깐 들렀습니다.
examples.trans: I stopped by briefly to drop off my bags before heading over.
This expression comes from 'stopped by'.

meanings.note: Used when repeating an action.

examples.trans: See you again!
It is raining again.

meanings.note: Action of coming together with someone.

examples.trans: I meet a friend.
Let's meet tomorrow.

meanings.note: Combines with 하다 in 말하다 (to speak, to say).

examples.trans: I don't know what you mean.
You speak Korean well.

meanings.note: colloquial contraction of 무엇; also used rhetorically to brush off a question

examples.trans: What are you doing now?
Why are you even asking something like that?

meanings.note: Placed before a verb to emphasize immediate action or result.
E.g., 바로 옆 ('right next to'), 바로 그 사람 ('that very person').

examples.trans: I'll start right away now.
The cafe is right in front of the school.

meanings.note: Literal meaning: steamed rice.
By extension, refers to a meal in everyday expressions like 밥 먹다 ('to eat a meal').

examples.trans: Have you eaten?
Today's lunch is delicious.
One moment please, let me swap the camera battery.
The topic of battery came up during this shoot.
Did you hear about this drinks or something?
I was busy today because of drinks or something.
Did you hear about this Ms.?
I was busy today because of Ms..

meanings.note: Expresses sudden realization, surprise, or hesitation.

examples.trans: Ah, yes.
Oh, I see!

meanings.note: casual greeting or farewell

examples.trans: Hi! Have you been well?
See you tomorrow, bye!

meanings.note: ㄹ-irregular verb: stem 알- drops ㄹ before ㄴ, ㅂ, ㅅ (e.g., 압니까)

examples.trans: Do you know that person's phone number?
Yes, I know well.

meanings.note: noun

examples.trans: Go forward.
Do well in the future.

meanings.note: Used as noun + subject (약속이).

examples.text: 아 신디 씨, 나 지금 약속이 있어서…
examples.trans: Ah Ms. Cindy, I actually have plans right now…
This point about plans, an appointment is really important.

meanings.note: Used to change the subject or brush off previous points.

examples.trans: Anyway, thank you.
I will try it anyway.

meanings.note: Sino-Korean word.

examples.trans: Let's go watch a movie.
What movie is it?

meanings.note: Used as noun + directional (영화관으로).

examples.text: 그래, 그럼 나는 집에 잠깐 가서 옷을 갈아입고 영화관으로 가지 뭐.
examples.trans: All right, then I will swing by home to change clothes and head to the movie theater.
This point about to the movie theater is really important.

meanings.note: Slightly more formal/deferential variant of 네, commonly used when speaking to a boss or superior.

examples.trans: Yes, understood.
Yes, I will prepare it right away.

meanings.note: The present day; often used adverbially without a particle.

examples.trans: The weather is nice today.
What day of the week is it today?

meanings.en: to come (of a feeling, state, or weather)
meanings.note: Used in expressions like 혼란이 오다 (confusion comes) or 비가 오다 (rain falls)

examples.text: 한국에 온 지 일 년 됐어요.
examples.trans: It's been one year since I came to Korea.
I suddenly started feeling sleepy.
The outfit you're wearing today is really pretty.
It's cold, so please wear warm clothes.

meanings.note: Used when wanting a noun/object.

examples.trans: What do you want?
We want peace.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (interj).

examples.trans: Yeah, she was pretty—and I asked her out for a second date too.
Here the word for 'yeah' is key.

있다.gloss: to exist, to have, to stay

meanings.en: to exist, to be (in a place)
meanings.note: Opposite of 없다.
Marks the possessed item with 이/가.

examples.trans: Do you have time?
Nobody is at home.

related.gloss: to not exist, to not have

meanings.en: for a moment; briefly; a second
meanings.note: Used to soften requests or indicate a very short duration.

examples.trans: Do you have a moment?
Just a second, I'll be right there.

meanings.note: Humble first-person singular pronoun used in polite speech.

examples.trans: I have an induction ceremony.
Follow me.

meanings.note: Transitive verb taking -을/를.

examples.trans: I prepared the presentation materials in advance.
The time spent preparing for a trip is also enjoyable.
What time is it now?
I'll leave right now.

meanings.note: Everyday spoken intensifier; can also function as a noun meaning 'the real thing'.

examples.trans: I'm really busy today.
Is that really delicious?
I'm on my way home right now.
On weekends I usually rest at home.

meanings.note: 처음부터 means 'from the start'

examples.trans: Let's start over from the beginning.
This is my first time coming to Seoul.

meanings.note: Primary meaning: a friend or peer.

meanings.en: that person / kid (referring to someone younger)
meanings.note: Older speakers often refer to a younger person or celebrity as 그 친구.

examples.trans: I watched a movie with a friend today.
That kid really sings well.

meanings.note: Hangul spelling of the English abbreviation PD, widely used in Korean broadcasting.

examples.trans: Who is the PD in charge of the new program?

examples.text: 그녀는 예능 피디가 되기 위해 시험을 준비했다.
examples.trans: She prepared for the exam to become a variety PD.

meanings.en: to do, to perform, to hold
meanings.note: Core verb; also combines with nouns to form verbs.

examples.trans: What are you doing right now?
We are holding a meeting today.

meanings.note: Compound of 하다 (to do) and 주다 (to give).

examples.trans: Please help me (do helping for me).
Please do this for me.
My office is close to home.
I go to work at the office at 9 a.m.
